newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 FALL ONE PCT ON PROFIT-TAKING, FUTURES.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 FALL ONE PCT ON PROFIT-TAKING, FUTURES.

text.p: The FTSE 100 lost one percent of its value on Friday as profit-taking set in following Thursday's rise to record levels, dealers said.
The index traded 50.9 points off to 5,035.9 at 1212 GMT. The September expiry futures contract fell 75 points to 5,050 having hit 5,031, with fair value seen around 15 points.
The FTSE 250 surged 59.5 points, or 1.29 percent, to 4,657.7 amid talk of selling FTSE futures to buy smaller-cap stocks.
Engineering and building stocks were favoured, with an upgrade on Blue Circle adding strength to the sector. Blue Circle gained 20p to 446-1/2p and RMC 35p to 1,107-1/2p.
Engineering stocks also made big gains, with sterling's retreat firmly at the forefront of the market's psyche.

The view that weaker sterling would decrease the threat to exporters, and that interest rates would not see another rise in the current cycle, helped GKN 39p up to 1,226-1/2p, British Aerospace 38-1/2p to 1,479p, Smiths Industries 34-1/2p to 868p and TI 24p to 617-1/2p.

Heavily weighted stocks, which have fuelled the FTSE 100's recent record rise, fell sharply. Zeneca lost 49-1/2p to 2,003 and Glaxo 33-1/2p to 1,292. Banks suffered also with Barclays 31-1/2p lower at 1,416p and Lloyds 31-1/2p down to 746-1/2p.
Currency and interest rate considerations aside, Severn Trent fell after Ofwat released plans to further competition in sewerage. The stock dipped 15-1/2p to 824-1/2p.

Rank gained 5p to 345p as joint brokers NatWest and BZW launched the company's 10 percent buy-back. Volume was nearly 44 million, making it heaviest traded stock after British Telecom, where more than 46 million shares changed hands.
Rio Tinto bucked the trend also, rising 29p to 1,055-1/2p, tracking a rise in the broader Australian market where the stock is traded.
The Dow is expected to open about 100 points lower.
